title: Telling Time & Parts of the Day
description: Read the clock, ask the time, and pair time expressions with accurate prepositions (at, in).
objectives: Ask and tell the time using 'o'clock', 'half past', 'quarter past', and 'quarter to'
Use prepositions of time accurately: 'at' with specific times/night, 'in' with parts of the day

vocabularyList.definition: The period of time between dawn and noon.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: I have the most energy in the morning.

vocabularyList.definition: The time from noon or lunchtime to evening.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: We have an English lesson in the afternoon.

vocabularyList.definition: The period of time at the end of the day, usually from about 6 PM to bedtime.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: They walk together in the evening.

vocabularyList.definition: The period of darkness in each twenty-four hours.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: It gets pleasantly cool at night.
The airport bus arrives at midnight.

vocabularyList.definition: Twelve o'clock in the middle of the day; midday.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: The office cafeteria opens at noon.

vocabularyList.definition: A period of time equal to sixty seconds.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: The bus arrives in ten minutes.

vocabularyList.definition: A period of time equal to sixty minutes.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: We study for one hour every evening.

vocabularyList.definition: Happening or done before the usual or expected time.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: He arrives early for all his interviews.

vocabularyList.definition: Doing something or taking place after the expected or usual time.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: Please do not be late for class.

sections.title: Telling the Time & Prepositions
sections.content:
To ask the time in English, say:
- **What time is it?** or **What's the time?**
- Always start the answer with: **It is... (It's...)**

### Clock Expressions
- Exact hour: *It's seven o'clock (7:00)*
- 15 minutes after: *It's quarter past seven (7:15)*
- 30 minutes after: *It's half past seven (7:30)*
- 15 minutes before the next hour: *It's quarter to eight (7:45)*

callouts.title: The Special Exception: Night
callouts.text: Notice: We say **in the morning**, **in the afternoon**, and **in the evening**, BUT we say **at night** (never 'in the night' for general time).

callouts.title: Never Use 'O'clock' with Minutes
callouts.text: Never say 'eight thirty o'clock'. O'clock is ONLY used for exact on-the-hour times (8:00).

sections.title: Lesson Summary
summaryPoints: Use 'at' for specific times: at 7:00, at half past eight, at noon, at midnight, at night.
Use 'in' for periods of the day: in the morning, in the afternoon, in the evening.
15 min past = quarter past; 30 min = half past; 15 min to = quarter to.
Only use 'o'clock' on the exact hour (7:00 -> 7 o'clock; never 7:30 o'clock).
AM = morning (midnight to noon); PM = afternoon/evening (noon to midnight).
